fields.value: etude check and etude guide: offline compiler-style experiment validator with inline fixes

Filed from f4109f exploration (scratch/roadmap.md, Part I / Auto-Research Lab).

## Outcome

Give both humans and coding agents a zero-network, compiler-style front door that validates an experiment file before spending a cent on GPUs:

1. **`etude check FILE.py` (read command — no provider key, no network):**
   - Validates experiment declarations, `train(config)`, `async def play` / `play_many` signatures (`EXP-77` / `6db832`), `Agents(load=, build=)` compatibility, heavy-import hygiene (`torch`/`mlx`/`jax` kept out of game modules), seed/budget sanity, and resolves the exact planned run/checkpoint/match summary.
   - Prints actionable inline fixes (`fix: ...`) directly beside each line number so an agent (or person) can repair errors in one pass without reading prose docs.
   - Supports machine-readable `--format json` and meaningful exit codes (aligning with `EXP-59`).
2. **`etude guide`:**
   - Prints a concise, always-up-to-date reference of Etude conventions, commands, and `check` -> `quote` -> `launch` -> `wait` workflow so coding agents do not need bespoke hand-maintained prompts.

## Notes & coordination

- Complements `EXP-59` (JSON output across commands) and `EXP-61` (standing human-set spending limits across launches under an experiment label).
- Share validation rules directly with declaration loading so `etude check` cannot drift from runtime acceptance.
